items.headline: SIRA bars a Central Coast physiotherapist and his practice from the NSW schemes, making their treatment unrecoverable from 14 August
items.summary: SIRA announced on 15 September that it has issued directions against a Central Coast physiotherapist and his physiotherapy company, removing them from the NSW workers compensation and motor accident schemes with effect from 14 August 2026 and barring the practitioner from any management or operational involvement in a physiotherapy business. Because SIRA approval is what makes a physiotherapist appropriately qualified for the purposes of the treatment-cost provisions in the Workers Compensation Act, anything delivered from that date sits outside the scheme regardless of when it is invoiced. SIRA also referred its concerns to Ahpra and the Health Professionals Council Authority, which has imposed conditions on the practitioner's registration.
items.so_what: Two exposures follow for insurers, scheme agents and employers: invoices already in the pipeline from this practice are not recoverable if the service date falls on or after 14 August, and any injured worker whose treatment was interrupted needs an alternative approved practitioner arranged before the recovery plan slips. The wider signal matters more than the individual case, because SIRA's register of directed providers holds only a handful of entries and the regulator reserves the power for sustained non-compliance, so its use here indicates the health-provider supervision model coming out of the Dawson strategic review is now operating in practice - and checking provider approval status is becoming a live control rather than an assumption.
